title: Inert factorization categories in a Cartesian cylinder
statement:
Use small quasicategories, coherent triangles, full subcategories, equivalences and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], Cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], symmetric infinity operads and inert edges of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition], and ordered join coslices of [lem-cbc-relative-coslice-left-fibration], with opposite join slices as in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence]. Let $p:P\to N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ be a symmetric infinity operad and $g:D\to P$ a categorical fibration (an inner fibration lifting equivalences with prescribed source). Let $u:E\to\Delta^1$ be a Cartesian fibration with degreewise endpoint fibres $E_0=P$ and $E_1=D$, such that every $d\in D$ is the target of a $u$-Cartesian edge $c_d:g(d)\to d$ over $0\to1$, and let $r:E\to P$ satisfy $r|_P=1_P$, $r|_D=g$, and carry all $u$-Cartesian edges to equivalences. For $x\in P$ put
$$K_x=D\times_E E_{x/},\qquad K'_x=D\times_P P_{x/}.$$
Let $I_x\subseteq K_x$ be full on arrows whose image under $r$ is inert in $P$, and $I'_x\subseteq K'_x$ full on inert arrows $x\to g(d)$. The map induced by $r$ is an equivalence $K_x\to K'_x$ over $D$ and restricts to an equivalence $I_x\to I'_x$. For $a\in K_x$ write $r(a)=(d,\alpha:x\to g(d))$. Set $B=P_{/g(d)}$ and let $F_g(d,\alpha)$ be the full subcategory of
$$D_{/d}\times_B B_{\alpha/}$$
on vertices $(\beta:d'\to d,\gamma:x\to g(d'),g(\beta)\gamma\simeq\alpha)$ with $\gamma$ inert; the maps to $B$ are induced by $g$ and by target evaluation. Then there are equivalences
$$(I_x)_{/a}\simeq(I'_x)_{/r(a)}\simeq F_g(d,\alpha).$$
Here $(I_x)_{/a}$ denotes the coherent comma category of arrows in $K_x$ from an object of $I_x$ to $a$, and similarly for $I'_x$. The equivalences retain all coherent comparisons, with no inertness requirement on $\beta$ or on morphisms between factorizations. Neither a unary-fibre equivalence nor weak contractibility of the factorization categories is assumed.
